name: Hoshea, last king of Israel
charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; conspiring with Egypt against Assyria
summary: Hoshea the son of Elah, last king of the northern kingdom, did evil though not as the kings before him. He became tributary to Assyria, then conspired with So king of Egypt and withheld tribute. Shalmaneser shut him in prison, besieged Samaria three years, and carried Israel away to Assyria.
offense: Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in the twelfth year of Ahaz and reigned nine years in Samaria. He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him (2 Kings 17:1–2). The qualification does not excuse his reign; it measures how far the standard had fallen when the best that could be said of a king was that he was less evil than his predecessors. Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid tribute. But the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and brought no present as he had done year by year (2 Kings 17:3–4). Instead of turning to the Lord, Hoshea turned to Egypt, the very nation from which the Lord had brought Israel out.
judgment: The king of Assyria shut Hoshea up and bound him in prison. He came up throughout all the land and besieged Samaria three years. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away, placing them in Halah, in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:4–6). The northern kingdom ceased to exist. The Lord removed Israel out of His sight, as He had said by all His servants the prophets (2 Kings 17:23). Every warning through every prophet sent to the northern kingdom was fulfilled in a single removal. The accumulated sin from Jeroboam through Hoshea was answered in captivity, and the tribes were scattered among the nations.

verses.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.

And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

text.text: Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.

entries.commentary: Hoshea son of Elah reigns nine years over Israel in Samaria and does evil, though not as the kings before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up, and Hoshea becomes his servant and pays tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped his yearly tribute, so he shuts him up in prison. Assyria besieges Samaria three years, then in the ninth year of Hoshea takes it and carries Israel away to Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes.

This captivity comes because the children of Israel sinned against the Most High who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods. They walked in the statutes of the heathen, built high places in all their cities, and set up images and groves on every high hill and under every green tree. They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing. -

The Most High testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, calling them to turn from evil and keep His commandments. They would not hear but hardened their necks like their fathers who did not believe in the Most High. To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments, so those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe. They rejected His statutes and covenant, followed vanity, made molten images and two calves, worshipped the host of heaven, and served Baal. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. -

The Most High is very angry and removes Israel out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah. Judah also fails to keep the commandments and walks in the statutes that Israel made. The Most High rejects all the seed of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hand of spoilers until He casts them out of His sight. This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there. -

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to dwell in the cities of Samaria in Israel's place. Because they do not fear the Most High, He sends lions among them that slay some of them. One of the carried-away priests is brought back to Bethel to teach the settlers how they should fear the Most High.

Every nation makes gods of its own and sets them in the houses of the high places the Samaritans had made. The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, Cuth made Nergal, Hamath made Ashima, the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children to Adrammelech and Anammelech. They feared the Most High and also served their own gods after the manner of the nations they came from. The Most High made His covenant and charged the children of Jacob whom He named Israel, showing the covenant belongs to Israel and not to all nations.

The Most High commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods, but to fear and worship Him alone who brought them out of Egypt with a stretched out arm. They were to observe His statutes, ordinances, and commandments forevermore, and He would deliver them out of the hand of all their enemies. No nation and no treaty can redeem Israel from their condition, only turning to the Most High can. These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. -
